Phase 2 independent synthetic fixture provenance

Newly authored local test source and synthetic vectors are placed in the existing
pask-wire Apache-2.0 lane. See LICENSING.md and crates/pask-wire/LICENSE.
This is not a new license grant for other preserved source or fixtures.

These fixtures are generated by generate.py using Python cbor2, hashlib and
OpenSSL-backed cryptography Ed25519, independently of the Rust candidate-entry
encoder, Merkle root reconstruction and signature verifier under test.
Run `python crates/pask-wire/tests/fixtures/phase2/generate.py --check` to reproduce
all 25 generated files without changing them. The generator source and this notice
are not themselves generated. manifest.json carries each generated binary SHA-256,
full expected roots/signatures and public deterministic TEST seeds.

No real Transparency Service, authenticated configuration channel, network service,
registration, hardware, physical event or ROS data was used. Receipt/statement
keys and data are local synthetic fixtures. A separately signed statement payload
is intentionally not a Pask application acceptance fixture. Its receipt subject
is issuer-defined and deliberately not the application site.id.

The Rust trust context uses an explicitly named LocalSimulation origin, a fake
caller-authenticated binding declaration and fixed evaluation time. A passing
ts_identity_trust in that mode is conditional simulation only; the report refuses
to pass acceptable_for_registration. One test exercises CallerAuthenticatedExternal
by an explicit caller assertion to test that API branch; it still is not observed
external authentication. The library does not authenticate provisioning.

Standards relevant to these local algorithms:
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.html#section-2.1
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9942.html#section-5.2
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9052.html#section-4.4
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9943.html#section-7.1
